question:
A 52-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, headaches, and type 2 diabetes mentions
during his routine physical examination that he experienced hives following
trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole treatment for cellulitis three years ago. He has expressed concern after
reading online that some medications used to treat his current conditions contain sulfa compounds.
Beyond advising him to avoid sulfonamide antimicrobial agents, what additional recommendation, if
any, should be made regarding medications to avoid? Answer Choices: (A) He should avoid all
sulfonamide-containing medications (B) He should avoid both sulfonamide antimicrobials and carbonic
anhydrase inhibitors (C) He need only avoid sulfonamide antimicrobial agents (D) He should avoid all
medications with a sulfonamide structure regardless of their therapeutic class (E) He should avoid all
medications that contain an SO2NH2 group (F) He should undergo allergy testing before taking any
sulfa-containing medications (G) He should avoid only medications that share the N1 substituent with
trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (H) He should avoid all medications with a sulfonyl functional group (I)
He should avoid all medications containing sulfur atoms (J) He should also avoid furosemide
 A. He should avoid all medications with a sulfonamide structure regardless of their therapeutic class
B. He should avoid all medications that contain an SO2NH2 group
C. He should also avoid furosemide
D. He should undergo allergy testing before taking any sulfa-containing medications
E. He should avoid only medications that share the N1 substituent with
trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
F. He need only avoid sulfonamide antimicrobial agents
G. He should avoid all medications with a sulfonyl functional group
H. He should avoid all medications containing sulfur atoms
I. He should avoid all sulfonamide-containing medications
J. He should avoid both sulfonamide antimicrobials and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
